findings.title: Inductive theme: 'Validation and Use of Competency Assessment Instruments in Engineering Education'
findings.description: Theme discovered via inductive analysis

evidence.theme: Validation and Use of Competency Assessment Instruments in Engineering Education
evidence.definition: The development, validation, and application of assessment tools such as scales, rubrics, or questionnaires to measure specific competencies, skills, or attitudes in engineering students. This includes statistical validation, expert judgment, and the use of these instruments in laboratory, project-based, or classroom settings.
subthemes: Psychometric validation of competency assessment instruments

findings.title: Inductive theme: 'Self-Efficacy and Learning Experiences in Engineering Education'
findings.description: Theme discovered via inductive analysis

evidence.theme: Self-Efficacy and Learning Experiences in Engineering Education
evidence.definition: The measurement of students' confidence or belief in their ability to perform specific tasks (self-efficacy) and the assessment of learning experiences (e.g., performance accomplishments, vicarious learning) that contribute to its development. This includes the exploration of how these factors influence career-related outcomes and affective traits in engineering contexts.
subthemes: Self-efficacy and attitudes in engineering contexts
Learning experiences and sources of self-efficacy

findings.title: Inductive theme: 'Professional, Ethical, and Generic Competencies in Engineering Education'
findings.description: Theme discovered via inductive analysis

evidence.theme: Professional, Ethical, and Generic Competencies in Engineering Education
evidence.definition: The assessment and development of non-technical or soft skills (e.g., communication, teamwork, leadership, problem-solving) alongside professional and ethical competencies in engineering students. This includes the evaluation of students' understanding and application of ethical standards, social responsibility, and professional conduct in engineering practice.
subthemes: Generic and professional competencies in engineering education
Assessment of professional and ethical competencies in engineering

findings.title: Inductive theme: 'Socio-Emotional and Psychological Competencies in Engineering Education'
findings.description: Theme discovered via inductive analysis

evidence.theme: Socio-Emotional and Psychological Competencies in Engineering Education
evidence.definition: The exploration and validation of socio-emotional and psychological constructs such as resilience, optimism, adaptability, compassion, and empathy in engineering education. This includes their impact on academic performance, retention, ethical reasoning, and overall success in engineering students.
subthemes: Resilience and psychological factors in engineering education
Compassion and socio-emotional competencies in engineering

findings.title: Inductive theme: 'Motivational and Career-Related Constructs in Engineering Education'
findings.description: Theme discovered via inductive analysis

evidence.theme: Motivational and Career-Related Constructs in Engineering Education
evidence.definition: The study of students' intrinsic and extrinsic motivations, attitudes, learning strategies, and career-related trajectories in engineering contexts. This includes the development of instruments to measure these constructs and the exploration of factors influencing career choices, intentions, and leadership development.
subthemes: Motivational attitudes and behaviors in engineering education
Career-related constructs and trajectories in engineering students

findings.title: Inductive theme: 'Representational Competence in Engineering'
findings.description: Theme discovered via inductive analysis

evidence.definition: The ability of students to interpret, switch between, and use multiple representations (e.g., diagrams, symbols, narrative language) of engineering concepts, particularly in problem-solving contexts. This competence is critical for conceptual understanding and effective communication in engineering.

findings.title: Inductive theme: 'Research Competencies in Engineering Education'
findings.description: Theme discovered via inductive analysis

evidence.definition: The assessment and development of research-related skills and competencies in engineering students, including investigative skills, scientific writing, and research training. These competencies encompass intellectual, technical, and communicative aspects of research projects.

findings.title: Inductive theme: 'Critical Thinking and Decision-Making in Engineering'
findings.description: Theme discovered via inductive analysis

evidence.theme: Critical Thinking and Decision-Making in Engineering
evidence.definition: The development and validation of instruments to assess critical thinking and decision-making competencies in engineering students. This often occurs in the context of specific technical or professional problem-solving scenarios.

findings.title: Inductive theme: 'Systems Thinking and Problem-Solving in Engineering'
findings.description: Theme discovered via inductive analysis

evidence.theme: Systems Thinking and Problem-Solving in Engineering
evidence.definition: The assessment of students' ability to approach complex engineering problems holistically, considering interdependencies and broader systems. This theme includes the development of tools to evaluate design mindset, iterative problem-solving, and competency in handling complex systems.

findings.title: Inductive theme: 'Impact of Experiential Learning on Engineering Student Outcomes'
findings.description: Theme discovered via inductive analysis

evidence.theme: Impact of Experiential Learning on Engineering Student Outcomes
evidence.definition: The exploration of how hands-on, real-world learning experiences such as internships, community-partnered projects, and apprenticeships influence the development of students' skills, self-efficacy, and professional readiness. This includes the assessment of workplace learning and its role in shaping career trajectories.

findings.title: Inductive theme: 'Gender Differences in Engineering Competencies and Self-Efficacy'
findings.description: Theme discovered via inductive analysis

evidence.theme: Gender Differences in Engineering Competencies and Self-Efficacy
evidence.definition: The exploration of differences between male and female engineering students in terms of self-efficacy, competencies, affective traits, and academic performance. This includes studies investigating gendered experiences, self-efficacy gaps, and their implications for engineering education and career outcomes.
subthemes: Self-efficacy gaps between male and female students
Impact of gender on academic performance and retention

findings.title: Inductive theme: 'Sustainability and Ethics Competencies in Engineering Education'
findings.description: Theme discovered via inductive analysis

evidence.theme: Sustainability and Ethics Competencies in Engineering Education
evidence.definition: The integration of sustainability, ethics, and social responsibility into engineering curricula, and the assessment of these competencies among engineering students. This theme includes the development of tools and frameworks to measure students' understanding and application of ethical principles and sustainability practices.
subthemes: Curricular integration of sustainability and ethics
Assessment of ethical reasoning in engineering

findings.title: Inductive theme: 'Innovation and Entrepreneurship Competencies in Engineering'
findings.description: Theme discovered via inductive analysis

evidence.theme: Innovation and Entrepreneurship Competencies in Engineering
evidence.definition: The measurement and development of innovation self-efficacy and entrepreneurial competencies among engineering students. This includes the creation and validation of scales to assess these competencies and their role in career development and engineering practice.

findings.title: Inductive theme: 'Measurement Invariance and Fairness in Engineering Education Assessments'
findings.description: Theme discovered via inductive analysis

evidence.theme: Measurement Invariance and Fairness in Engineering Education Assessments
evidence.definition: The examination of whether assessment instruments function similarly across different subpopulations of engineering students, such as first-generation college students or underrepresented groups. This theme includes studies on fairness, equity, and the development of inclusive assessment practices in engineering education.

findings.title: Inductive theme: 'Metacognitive and Learning Orientation Tools in Engineering Education'
findings.description: Theme discovered via inductive analysis

evidence.theme: Metacognitive and Learning Orientation Tools in Engineering Education
evidence.definition: The creation and validation of tools designed to measure metacognitive skills, learning orientations, and self-regulated learning among engineering students. This theme includes the development of instruments to assess how students plan, monitor, and evaluate their own learning processes in engineering contexts.
